newsitem.title: USA: Dominion seeks to cut regulatory assets.
newsitem.headline: Dominion seeks to cut regulatory assets.

text.p: Virginia Power's rate freeze proposal seeks to reduce the utility's regulatory assets by $500 million over the five years of the freeze, spokesman Dan Genest told Reuters.
The Dominion Resources Inc subsidiary now estimates its regulatory assets at $800 million, spokesman Bill Byrd said.
The utility proposes to recover the $300 million left after the first phase of its alternative regulation plan through the Transition Cost Charge proposed for the second phase of the plan, he said.
Byrd noted the company's estimates of its regulatory assets -- or potential stranded costs -- do not include the cost of purchasing power from independent, unregulated power producers.
Genest said any portion of the $500 million not recovered during the first five years of its alternative regulation plan would be written off.

To recover these costs during the rate freeze, he said, Virginia Power proposed allowing its return on equity to rise to 13 percent, with any return between 11.5 percent and 13 percent being used to reduce regulatory assets.
This is based on raising the company's allowed return on equity to 11.5 percent from the current 11.4 percent, Genest said.
He said the Virginia Power proposal filed with state regulators Monday also calls for any earnings above a 13 percent return on equity being shared equally between rate payers and the utility.
Asked about the company's actual return on equity, Byrd said "We are very close" to the current allowed level of 11.4 percent. ((-- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.))
